newsitem.title: USA: Republic says judge freezes car dealer deal.
newsitem.headline: Republic says judge freezes car dealer deal.

text.p: Republic Industries Inc said Monday that an administrative law judge from the Texas Department of Transportation has denied its request to lift a stay of its pending acquisition of Joe Myers Toyota of Houston, Texas.

The stay was imposed automatically when Toyota Motors USA filed an action with the department, in which Toyota, a unit of the Japanese car company, is seeking to block its acquisition of the dealership, Republic said in a statement.
Responding to the decision, the Toyota unit said, "The judge's decision is a decisive victory for Texas consumers, as well as for Toyota and our dealers."

Republic, in its statement, said that in her ruling, Administrative Law Judge Molly Singletary ordered that the stay remain in effect until the Texas Motor Vehicle Board makes a final determination regarding the proposed acquisition of Joe Myers Toyota.
Republic's president and co-chief executive officer Steven R. Berrard said Republic was "disappointed but not surprised by this decision."

He noted that the process before the Texas Motor Vehicle Board is in its early stages and that Republic believes it will ultimately "prevail in our effort to make acquisitions without regard to Toyota's arbitrary policies."
"Republic remains committed to its strategy and will pursue every means to execute that strategy," he said.

"We tried to get the stay lifted because we believe we will ultimately prevail on the merits, but it's important to remember that the judge's decision to keep the stay in place does not in any way lend credibility to Toyota's original complaint," he said.
